 Anwar tells AG to seek audience with King over Najib's conditional pardon
 By Charles Ramendran 
 Saturday, 07 Nov 2026
 | 5:54 PM MYT

 SHAH ALAM: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar to seek an audience with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, to explain the legal complications surrounding the implementation of former premier Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest order.
 Anwar said the the Attorney General's Chambers (AGC) faced legal constraints due to Najib's separate 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case. "The issue is the second case involving 1MDB, where Najib has not been granted bail. The judiciary needs to finalise this matter. It is not within my powers.
 "His Majesty has made a decision and we as the people must respect and comply with it, while understanding the Federal Constitution and the powers vested in the Yang di-Pertuan Agong," he said after launching the November National Family Month 2026 here on Saturday (Nov 7).
 Anwar said he had instructed Mohd Dusuki to promptly seek an audience with His Majesty to explain why the pardon had been accepted in the SRC case but difficulties had arisen over its implementation in relation to the 1MDB case.
 He said the matter would take a few days to resolve after consultations with the judiciary.
 Anwar added that the AG has sought an audience with His Majesty.
 "I do not want to politicise this matter, but I want to make it clear that the powers of His Majesty are not in dispute. This issue has arisen because of the second case involving 1MDB and whether the conditional pardon in the SRC case can be implemented. This is for the AGC and the judiciary to clarify," he said.
 Anwar said he would leave it to the AGC to provide further details and stressed that the matter was not within the Prime Minister's authority to determine.
 Najib was granted a conditional pardon that reduced his 12-year jail sentence in the SRC International case to six years and his RM210mil fine to RM50mil. The pardon also allowed him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. However, the implementation of the order has run into complications because Najib is also serving a separate 15-year jail sentence following his conviction in the 1MDB case. The AGC has sought clarification on the legal implications and denied defying or challenging the conditional royal pardon.
